title: Integrated Security & Compliance Controlbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk Exceptions
author: Mariana Lopez
content:
Overview:
This controlbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s operational requirements and prescriptive procedures for RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for service owners, platform engineers, security reviewers, and compliance owners.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: applies to all Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane components, and customer Private deployments where Redwood manages the control plane.
- Intent: provide a single reference that maps controls to owners, SLOs/thresholds, evidence artifacts, and step-by-step procedures for common workflows.

Quick summary of responsibilities:
- Security team: policy definitions, control validation, exceptions approvals, audit orchestration.
- Eng SRE/Platform: implement RBAC/telemetry, configure logging pipelines, enforce retention.
- Service owners: maintain service-level ACLs, attest to data residency, produce evidence for audits.
- Legal/Compliance: intake and sign-off for long-term retention and exception justification.

1) RBAC & Authentication (AuthN/AuthZ)
Purpose: ensure least-privilege access across dev, staging, and production.
Principles:
- Centralized identity (Okta) for human users and short-lived OIDC tokens for CI/service accounts.
- AuthZ enforced via two layers: platform-wide coarse-grained roles (IAM groups) + fine-grained service-level RBAC (OPA + internal rbac-service).
- Secrets and signing keys remain in Vault (HashiCorp).

Primary services and ownership:
- Identity provider: Okta (security owns policy and SCIM integration).
- Platform permissions: AWS IAM + GCP IAM (eng-infra owns role lifecycle).
- Fine-grained service RBAC: rbac-service (eng-platform owns schema & enforcement).
- Policy evaluation: Open Policy Agent (policy repo: github.com/redwood/security/policies, security owns reviews).

Standard roles (table):
- Role: admin | Scope: org-wide | Allowed actions: full policy management, infra create/delete | Owner: security
- Role: platform-operator | Scope: production infra | Allowed actions: deploy, scale, troubleshoot | Owner: eng-sre
- Role: service-owner | Scope: single-service | Allowed actions: change config, approve releases | Owner: service team
- Role: read-only | Scope: visibility | Allowed actions: dashboards, logs read | Owner:eng-platform

Onboarding & offboarding checklist (numbered):
1. Provision Okta account and assign groups based on least privilege.
2. Create IAM bindings and service account with minimal permissions.
3. Issue short-lived credentials (OIDC) for CI through GitHub Actions/OIDC.
4. Register service in rbac-service and map roles to policies.
5. Document owner and SLA in service registry.
6. Offboarding: remove Okta access, revoke sessions, rotate affected secrets.

RBAC audit & periodic attestation:
- Quarterly: service owners must attest to list of principals with privileged access (owner email + timestamp).
- Automated monthly report: list of role bindings with >90-day unused access flagged.
- Alerts: >100 failed credential attempts in 5 minutes for a service triggers security paging.

2) Audit Logging & Observability
Goal: maintain tamper-resistant logs for security events, enable fast investigations, and satisfy regulatory retention windows.
What we log (minimum):
- Auth events: login, logout, token issuance, token revocation, SCIM provisioning.
- Privileged actions: role changes, policy updates, IAM updates, Vault secrets access (access log).
- Platform actions: deployments, DB schema migrations, data export requests.
- Administrative console access and failed/successful attempts.

Pipeline and storage:
- Primary ingestion: Datadog Logs (realtime monitoring and alerting).
- Long-term archive: S3 (encrypted with AWS KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/redwood-compliance) with object locks for WORM where required.
- Evidence index: ElasticSearch cluster for audit queries (read-only replicas for compliance reviewers).

Retention and retention configuration table:
- Type: AuthN/AuthZ logs | Retention: 1 year (hot in Datadog 90d, archive S3 12mo) | Rationale: operational + SOC 2
- Type: Change control & privileged ops | Retention: 3 years | Rationale: contractual/legal
- Type: Customer data access logs (per-customer residency) | Retention: per-customer policy (default 1 year) | Rationale: data residency requirements

Tamper-resistance and verification:
- All archived logs are encrypted and signed with KMS; bucket policies deny delete unless request approved by compliance.
- Monthly integrity checks: compute SHA256 manifests of daily archives, store manifests in separate KMS-protected bucket and a copy in an offline vault (eng-security runbook).

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- Unusual policy change: any org-role binding change outside business hours => PagerDuty P2 to security oncall.
- High-rate Vault access: >500 secret access events from a single principal in 1 hour => P1 investigation.

3) Data Residency & Retention
Residency controls:
- Customer data is tagged at ingestion with data_residency: {region}. Service must declare allowed regions in service registry.
- Redwood hosted: default region us-east-1 (primary) with eu-west-1 for EU-customer data. Private deployments follow customer-managed region.

Encryption:
- At rest: AES-256; keys managed in AWS KMS (customer-managed key for Private).
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ (prefer TLS 1.3).

Retention policy (default):
- Non-sensitive telemetry: 90 days hot, 2 years archive.
- Auth and audit logs: see Audit section.
- Customer PII: retention only as contract requires; default is 90 days unless customer contract states otherwise.

Data deletion and evidence of deletion (procedure):
1. Service owner opens data deletion request in the compliance portal (link: /internal/compliance/data-deletion).
2. Infra runs purge job scoped to tenant-id with governor to prevent over-deletion.
3. System generates deletion evidence bundle (manifest + sha256) stored in evidence S3 prefix s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/deletions/<tenant-id>/<timestamp>.json.
4. Compliance confirms and records deletion in audit log.

4) Secure SDLC Controls
Goal: shift-left security, ensure code and third-party components meet minimum bar before production.
Required gates (applies to all services):
- Code review: 2 engineer approvals for production changes.
- Static analysis: Snyk/Trivy/Semgrep scan must pass critical/high findings remediated or a documented exception exists.
- Dependency policy: no usage of packages with known critical vulnerabilities; automated dependency updates via Renovate.
- Secrets scanning: git-secrets and pre-commit hooks; failing commit blocks merge.
- Runtime policy checks: infra-as-code plan review and policy-as-code (OPA) gate for infra changes.

Developer tooling and integrations:
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions with enforced branch protections.
- SAST/DAST: scans run on PR (SAST) and weekly in mainline (DAST).
- Threat modeling: required for services handling sensitive data; model template in /security/threat-models.

Evidence artifacts for audits:
- PR history with approvals, CI run IDs, scan result snapshot (JSON), dependency SBOM (CycloneDX), and threat model PDF.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
Purpose: provide a repeatable, prioritized response for security incidents.
Incident classification and initial actions:
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev 1 (P0): Active data exfiltration, customer-impacting data integrity loss, production-wide compromise. Response: full incident SCRUM, 24/7 war room, executive notification within 30 minutes.
  - Sev 2 (P1): Targeted service compromise or privileged access misuse. Response: security-led triage, containment, mitigation plan within 2 hours.
  - Sev 3 (P2): Low-impact vulnerability exploitation, suspicious activity. Response: normal on-call handling, investigation within 24 hours.

Security runbook (numbered):
1. Detect: alerts from Datadog, IDS, or external reports.
2. Triage: security oncall assesses scope, containment needs, and severity.
3. Contain: disable compromised accounts, revoke tokens, rotate keys (Vault rotation playbook).
4. Investigate: capture forensic artifacts (memory/host snapshots, logs, network pcaps), preserve chain-of-custody.
5. Remediate: implement fixes, validate with tests, and plan for rollback if needed.
6. Communicate: internal slack channel #incidents, status page update (if customer-impacting), and exec brief.
7. Postmortem: publish RCA within 7 business days and a remediation plan with owners.

Forensic evidence handling:
- Evidence are stored in forensics bucket s3://redwood-forensics/<incident-id>/ with restricted ACLs and retention per legal.
- Access requires approval from security incident lead and is logged to the audit pipeline.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose: ensure audit readiness with repeatable artifacts and owner responsibilities.
Standard evidence catalog (examples):
- Control: RBAC attestations | Artifact: quarterly attestation spreadsheet (signed) | Owner: service-owner
- Control: Secure SDLC | Artifact: PR snapshots, SBOM, SAST/DAST reports | Owner: eng-developer-experience
- Control: Audit logs | Artifact: log retention manifests, S3 object manifests | Owner: eng-platform
- Control: Incident handling | Artifact: incident report, chain-of-custody | Owner: security

Evidence lifecycle process (numbered):
1. Evidence generation: automated where possible (CI artifacts, log manifests).
2. Evidence storage: canonical evidence must be copied to s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/<control>/<year>/<service>/.
3. Evidence indexing: compliance-runbook job indexes artifacts into the evidence catalog (metadata stored in Confluence index + compliance DB).
4. Audit request: compliance sends a request with required artifacts; owners have 10 business days to provide.
5. Audit response: compliance attaches artifacts and submits to auditor; any missing artifacts trigger remediation plan.

7) Risk & Exceptions
Process for requesting a controlled exception:
1. Submit exception request in the exception tracker (link: /internal/compliance/exceptions) with risk assessment, compensating controls, and TTL (maximum 90 days without renewal).
2. Security reviews risk and either rejects, approves with conditions, or defers to Legal/Compliance.
3. Approved exceptions require mitigation plan, monitoring, and an owner assigned.
4. Renewals: must be submitted 14 days before expiry.

Exception approval criteria (short list):
- Business criticality and impact if blocked.
- Compensating controls that reduce risk to acceptable levels (e.g., enhanced monitoring, IP allowlists, reduced scope).
- Sunset plan and measurable milestones.

8) Metrics & Reporting
Key metrics tracked weekly:
- % services with current RBAC attestations (target >= 95%).
- Number of active exceptions and average time-to-closure (target < 30 days).
- Mean time to detection (MTTD) for security incidents (target < 1 hour).
- Integrity check failures on archived logs (target 0).

Reporting cadence:
- Weekly security dashboard to executive and eng leaders.
- Quarterly compliance readiness review with Legal and Finance.

9) Related runbooks and links
- Vault rotation playbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/vault-rotation
- Forensics collection: /confluence/security-and-compliance/forensics-collection-runbook
- Evidence index job: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/evidence-indexer
- Threat model template: /confluence/security-and-compliance/threat-model-template

Appendix: Common checklist for new service launch (short):
- RBAC mapped and tested in staging.
- Logs shipped to Datadog and archival enabled.
- Encryption & KMS keys provisioned.
- CI gates configured (SAST, secret scan).
- Threat model completed (if applicable).
- Data residency declared in service registry.
- Compliance evidence path configured.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Security team (Mariana Lopez)
- Review cadence: annual full review, quarterly minor updates or after any major incident or regulation change.

Contact: security@redwood.example.com for questions or to initiate an exception request.
